en.text: Agave parrasana, the cabbage head agave or cabbage head century plant, is a flowering plant in the family Asparagaceae. A slow-growing evergreen succulent from North East Mexico, it produces a compact rosette of fleshy thorn-tipped grey-green leaves, 60 cm (24 in) tall and wide. The leaves are blue green and the thorns are red. The whole plant may reach 100 cm (39 in) tall and wide. Occasionally, mature plants produce a spectacular flower head up to 6 m (20 ft) tall, opening red and turning yellow. This signals the death of the flowering rosette. However, offsets may form and continue growing.
